clue.text: Left one kind of mammal means of escape

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a feline is a member of the cat family, one kind of mammal

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a type of animal while looking for a way out.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeline is a rope thrown to rescue someone, and figuratively any route out of trouble.

clue.text: Name of Aussie inhabitant poet used, confusing us Poms

definitions.text: Name of Aussie inhabitant poet used
definitions.note: T. S. Eliot called himself Old Possum, and a possum is an Australian marsupial

indicators.note: confusing the letters of the two words scrambles them into a new order

explanation.surface: An Australian creature's name, used by a poet, baffles the English (Poms is Aussie slang for Britons).
explanation.walkthrough: T. S. Eliot wrote Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, the source of the musical Cats, so the definition ties into the cat theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The possum is a marsupial native to Australia, and Old Possum was the nickname Eliot adopted as a poet.

clue.text: Change order for Manx cat re mice as dessert

indicators.note: to change the order of letters is to rearrange them into a new word
a Manx cat famously has no tail, so the word cat loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap a tailless cat's menu from mice to pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' docks the tail of cat, leaving CA; add RE MICE and rearrange the eight letters as 'Change order for' instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen sweet served as a pudding after the main course.

clue.text: In trouble, a cheetah appears to turn white

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follow, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A cheetah in distress seems to go pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears to' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleach is to lose colour and become pale, as cloth does in strong sunlight.

clue.text: eg Owl pursuing pussycat that's possibly ours, grabbing it

indicators.note: grabbing means the shuffled letters hold the next word within them
possibly signals that the letters of ours may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Edward Lear's Owl courts the Pussycat, perhaps our own cat, and holds on to it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lear's poem The Owl and the Pussy-cat, the Owl woos and marries the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman, as the Owl courts the Pussy-cat with a ring.

clue.text: Catty comment, say, that's inconsequential

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a snub or insult, of which a catty remark is an example
second meaning: small, trivial, of little importance

explanation.walkthrough: One meaning is a noun (an insult), the other an adjective (minor).
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a disparaging remark, while slight as an adjective means trivial or minor.

clue.text: Author backed deal, getting fur from American native

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the author's name runs in the other direction

parts.note: Umberto Eco, Italian author of The Name of the Rose
a lot, as in a great deal

explanation.surface: A writer supports a bargain and comes away with a pelt from the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild cat of Central and South America, once heavily hunted for its spotted pelt.

clue.text: Male twins that may be soundly beaten?

indicators.note: twins means the male word appears a second time, side by side

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Two boy twins who might well deserve a good hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly beaten' looks like a thrashing; it means struck to make a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a hand-beaten drum, so it is beaten to produce sound.

clue.text: Convert you mentored, producing book from OT

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious convert you trained, yielding a book of the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Deuteronomy is also a cat in Eliot's poems and the musical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuteronomy is the fifth book of the Old Testament, one of the five books of Moses.

clue.text: Tenacious types good to have in rows

indicators.note: to have in means the rows enclose the abbreviation inside them

parts.note: tiers are rows placed one above another

explanation.surface: Determined people are worth seating in the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigers are used figuratively for fierce, determined fighters who never give up.

clue.text: Former cat lover initially objects and cries out

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: aims are goals or objectives

explanation.surface: Someone who used to love cats raises objections and protests loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to shout suddenly in surprise or strong emotion.

clue.text: Recalled Siamese couple in pronouncement

indicators.note: in pronouncement means the word is taken as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: to tie is to join or couple together

explanation.surface: Remembering a pair of Siamese cats in an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reads as remembered, but means re-called, named again: Siam was renamed Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam became Thailand, so what was once called Siamese is now Thai.

clue.text: Not the same husband, in emotional state that can involve having kittens

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the emotional state

parts.note: a mood is a temporary state of feeling
other means different, not the same

explanation.surface: A new husband puts someone in an emotional state, the kind that brings on panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having kittens' is British slang for panicking, but here it is taken literally for a mother cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherhood is the condition of being a parent, which for a cat means bearing a litter.

clue.text: In unusually old home, trap insect spotted in Europe

indicators.note: unusually signals an odd arrangement of the letters in the three words

explanation.surface: An odd trap set in an old house catches a bug seen on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as sighted, but also describes the moth's spotty wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard moth is a European moth with white wings dotted with black spots.

clue.text: Write about match for colour of beautiful boat couple used

definitions.text: colour of beautiful boat couple used

indicators.note: about means the writing word wraps around the matching word

parts.note: to pen is to write
to agree is to match or correspond

explanation.surface: Writing about a pairing, to describe the shade of a lovely boat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lear's poem, the Owl and the Pussy-cat went to sea in a beautiful pea-green boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea green is a bright yellowish-green, the shade of the boat in Lear's verse.

clue.text: From island in Pacific ring America like a scaredy-cat

parts.note: Timor is an island in the Malay Archipelago, at the Pacific's western edge
O is shaped like a ring
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A frightened creature from an island travels on round the Pacific to America.
explanation.definitionFit: Timorous means fearful and nervous, as a scaredy-cat is easily frightened.

clue.text: Put foot repeatedly in fruit tree

indicators.note: repeatedly means the foot word is given a second time

parts.note: to paw is to put a foot on something, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone keeps stepping into a fruit tree, or a cat pawing at one.
explanation.definitionFit: The pawpaw is a tropical tree bearing papaya, or a North American tree with edible fruit.

clue.text: One having systematic way to do things, hunting animal

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a usual method of working
a user is one who has the use of something

explanation.surface: An animal with a methodical approach to hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat valued for catching mice, a hunter by trade.

clue.text: Diagnostic aid that'll help you see today's theme?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a medical body scanner

definitions.text: that'll help you see today's theme
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: a device for examining cats, the puzzle's theme

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, playful reading: a scanner for cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A CAT scanner uses computerised axial tomography to image the body, and the name contains the theme animal.

clue.text: Feed young awful clues about kitten's head

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters wrap around the single letter
awful clues are badly made, so their letters are reworked
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A setter's poor clues concern feeding a young cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns CLUES into SUCLE, and 'about' wraps that round K, the head of kitten's.
explanation.definitionFit: To suckle is to nurse infants or young animals with milk from the breast.

clue.text: Rotter that retains cat's haul?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nasty person, chiefly Australian and British slang
second meaning, whimsical: a sack holding rats a cat has caught

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading of the slang term: a bag of rats.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratbag is a despicable or troublesome person, a rogue or scoundrel.

clue.text: Speech in Cats? Tipsy, forgetting lines in middle

indicators.note: forgetting means the lines are left out of the word for tipsy
in middle says the dropped letters sit at the centre of the word

parts.note: mellow means pleasantly drunk
L is an abbreviation for line, so two of them is LL

explanation.surface: An actor in the musical Cats, a little drunk, forgets lines halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speech in Cats' sounds like dialogue in the show, but it is the sound cats make.
explanation.definitionFit: A meow is the cry a cat utters, its kind of talking.

clue.text: Small tame animal swallowing cold drink that's colourful

indicators.note: swallowing means the animal takes the cold abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a pet is a domesticated animal
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A little pet laps up a chilly drink of many colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is the band of colours made when light is split, as in a rainbow.

clue.text: Lively party, hit with cat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal British for a wild party
second meaning: to beat, as with a cat-o'-nine-tails whip

explanation.walkthrough: The cat here is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip once used for flogging.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrash means both a riotous celebration and to beat someone severely.

clue.text: Less domesticated, runs after writer

indicators.note: after means the runs abbreviation comes behind the writer's name

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, Irish playwright and wit
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Runs scored after a writer has a less tame feel.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilder means more untamed, like animals not kept as pets.

clue.text: We hear you are on spree in classic sports car

indicators.note: on means the spoken part follows the spree word

parts.note: a jag is a bout of indulgence, a spree

indicators.note: We hear means the following words are taken by their sound alone

parts.note: you are said aloud is like the letters U R, spoken as you-are

explanation.surface: Told that you are out on a binge in a vintage roadster.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a big cat, in keeping with the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaguar is a British car maker famed for sporting models like the E-type.
